messages.author: b09694a7dca08b64
messages.subject: Persistent variable problem -- I *think* I'm defining it in the right scope, but not working
parts:
I'm sorry if this a simple question, but I'm rather new to both R *and* Shiny -- the problem is that I think I'm defining a variable in the proper scope to be persistent for a session, but it isn't acting like that.

I'm trying to allow the user to build up a list of selected staff members, on whom analysis will be done. The complete staff list is in an Excel document, and as the user enters a partial name of the staff member, the Shiny UI will display staff that match, and when the user activates an Action button, the staff member will be appended to a persistent list, which will feed later analysis.

So far, I have the staff selection working nicely, but I seem to be unable to append to the persistent list. Could anyone tell me what I'm doing wrong?

I'm also concerned about how I'll handle the Action button, as I will be needing to track when it "increases" each time it is pressed.

Initially, I was trying to be fancy and using renderUI to have the Action button ONLY show up when the search criteria yielded only 1 hit, but since I couldn't even get the persistent list to build up, I removed that part. I do hope to add this back in later on.

# ui.R
shinyUI(fluidPage(

    sidebarLayout(
        sidebarPanel(
            textInput("searchtext", label = "Search staff", value = ""),
            actionButton("action", label = "Add to list")
        ),
       
        mainPanel(
            fluidRow( column( 6, verbatimTextOutput("hitlist") ) ),
            fluidRow( column( 6, verbatimTextOutput("history") ) )
        )
    )
))

# server.R

library(xlsx)
staff <- read.xlsx("peoplelist.xlsx", sheetIndex = 1, header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) # will search on "Name" column

shinyServer(
    function(input, output) {

        buildhistory <- c() # supposed to be persistent data for each user session
        oldaction <- 0
       
        output$hitlist <- renderText({
            result <- grep( input$searchtext, staff$Name, ignore.case = TRUE ) # returns indexes of matches; unique if length(result) == 1
            numberhits <- length(result)
            if ( numberhits == 0 ) {
                "No matches"
            } else if ( numberhits == 1 ) {
                staff$Name[result]
            } else { # multiple hits -- display all the hits, to a maximum of 20
                if ( numberhits > 20 ) {
                    result <- result[1:20]
                }
                paste(staff$Name[result], collapse = '\n', sep = '')
            }
        })
       
        output$history <- renderText({
            if (input$action != oldaction) {
                oldaction <- input$action
                buildhistory <- append(buildhistory, "add another") # this seems to run ONLY once?!? no appending happening...
            }
            paste(buildhistory, collapse = '*', sep = '')
        })
       
})

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Persistent variable problem -- I *think* I'm defining it in the right scope, but not working
parts:
1) I'd move the "input$action != oldaction" block out of output$history, and into a separate observe({...}). Let output$history focus on rendering that text.

2) buildhistory here is just a normal R variable, not a reactive one. Shiny's reactive expressions and outputs only know to calculate when their reactive dependencies change; it doesn't magically know what R variables are interesting to reactivity. You can add this call right before or after you first declare buildhistory: makeReactiveBinding("buildhistory"). Or if you have a bunch of reactive values to read/write, you could consider using reactiveValues() instead; it declares a list-like object where reading/writing values to it triggers reactivity.

3) The statement "buildhistory <- append(buildhistory, ...)" will trigger an endless chain reaction. You need to do this: "buildhistory <- append(isolate(buildhistory), ...)" so that your observe() block knows that it doesn't want to automatically re-execute when buildhistory changes (since it, itself, is about to change buildhistory).

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Persistent variable problem -- I *think* I'm defining it in the right scope, but not working
parts:
It's probably just the normal R scoping behavior you're seeing.

a <- 10
makeReactiveBinding("a")
a <- 20 # does trigger reactivity
foo <- function() {
  a <- 30 # doesn't trigger reactivity; this just creates a NEW variable inside this function's scope
  a <<- 30 # this does assign our original variable and triggers reactivity
}
foo()

Render expressions, observers, reactive expressions, etc. all introduce their own scopes just like functions do, so if you want to assign to variables in parent scopes you need to use <<-.
